new_public_evidence.source: Wang & Ramdas, Anytime-valid t-tests and confidence sequences for Gaussian means with unknown variance
new_public_evidence.result: The paper gives a shifted scale-invariant t-test martingale terminal factor for any fixed null mean and unknown variance, a canonical-filtration universal-inference t e-process, and an explicit warning that a value stopped using a finer filtration need not itself be an e-value suitable for multiplication.

new_public_evidence.source: Grunwald, de Heide & Koolen, Safe Testing
new_public_evidence.result: Study-level optional continuation is valid when each new factor is a conditional e-variable given prior studies. The paper explicitly warns that filtration mistakes in the t-test setting can create fake conditional e-variables with conditional expectation above one.

derived_results.claim: A one-sample t e-value cannot simply replace its fixed null mean by the random frozen reference mean and then be reused over future blocks. Conditional on the reference, future null data still have true mean mu0, not Xbar_ref. Marginal e-validity is insufficient for repeated same-reference multiplication.

Reference uncertainty can instead be protected by a frozen confidence interval I_R. For deterministic block length m, E_t=inf_{u in I_R}G_m^(c,u) is conditionally e-valid on the event mu0 in I_R because E_t<=G_m^(c,mu0) pointwise and the latter has expectation one for every null variance. Closed form uses only block mean, centered SSE and distance from block mean to I_R.

The CI-inf t factor is the same current-block multiplier for every delayed start, so the r82 telescoping heavy-tail start mixture still collapses to one scalar recursion per sign direction. Fixed deterministic block boundaries are required; arbitrary within-block peeking is not exported as an e-value.

With c=2.7 selected on separate discovery randomness, an independent 600-path-per-direction common-random validation on 11 exact Gaussian KL=1 directions improved worst tested q90 raw delay versus the current exponential mean factor while keeping variance channels and total conditional alpha unchanged.
derived_results.scope: Finite engineering grid only; no PFA inference from simulation and no continuum delay guarantee.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The result does not validate a random-reference plug-in safe-t factor; it validates an interval-infimum fixed-block factor.
Fixed deterministic block termination is essential because reduced-filtration stopped t-martingale values need not be e-values for downstream multiplication.
The validation covers an exact-KL=1 finite Gaussian grid and a worst reference envelope, not KL>=1 continuum, non-Gaussian data, dependence, gradual drift or repeated changes.
A finite-sample power theorem over the full moderate-variance Gaussian KL region remains open.

candidate_new.mechanism: Replace the two confidence-bound exponential mean channels in the r82 Gaussian delayed-start guard by deterministic-block scale-invariant t terminal factors minimized over the frozen reference mean confidence interval. Keep the variance likelihood channels and O(1) telescoping delayed-start recursion unchanged.
candidate_new.status: conditional type-I/common-increment proof closed inside fixed iid Gaussian block scope; independent finite-grid latency improvement observed; continuum high-probability delay proof pending

frontier: Derive a finite-sample high-probability lower bound for cumulative log CI-inf t evidence over the full Gaussian KL>=1 moderate-variance region using the joint noncentral-t/chi-square geometry rather than independent minimum-shift/maximum-variance rectangular bounds.

If the bound certifies lower or equal worst delay than the current exponential mean factor under the same reference and alpha accounting, promote the t-block replacement; otherwise keep it engineering-only.

Derive a canonical universal-inference block factor q_pred(block)/sup_{(mu,sigma) in frozen null confidence set}p_{mu,sigma}(block) and compare its growth to the CI-inf scale-invariant t factor. Preserve a proper predictive numerator and a common block increment across delayed starts.

Replace symbolic/high-precision Gaussian quantile constants in the retained variance/reference layer with true directed-rounding interval enclosures if a rigorous special-function implementation is available; otherwise keep exact symbolic quantiles authoritative.
Only after the Gaussian fixed-block theorem is closed, test the confidence-set-infimum/common-increment pattern in another exponential family with a fresh family-specific e-value proof.

Attempt a certified worst-direction reduction; if no analytic monotonicity closes, build a discovery/independent-validation continuum certificate.
